name: Bread Pudding
subtitle: stale bread, milk and dried fruit baked into the household dessert

ingredients.note: stale is not a compromise, fresh bread turns to paste

prepNotes: Every Anglo-Indian household made this and no two made it the same way. What is constant is stale bread, milk and whatever dried fruit was in the tin.
Soak the bread properly. Twenty minutes, not five.

steps.text: Warm the milk with the sugar until it dissolves. Pour it over the torn bread and leave 20 minutes.
Mash the soaked bread roughly with a fork. It should be lumpy, not smooth.
Beat in the eggs, melted butter, cardamom and nutmeg, then fold in the raisins and apricot.
Pour into a greased dish and bake at 180C for 50 minutes until set with a browned top and a slight wobble at the centre.
steps.tip: A slight wobble. Baked until firm all through, it is dry.

steps.text: Cool 20 minutes before cutting. It firms as it settles.

storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated. Serve at room temperature or warmed. It contains egg and milk, so keep it cold rather than on the counter.
